title: The Mind Can Transform Karma
author: Karma Cannot Bind the Mind
excerpt: To replace it with the Buddha-name is to transform karma through the mind.

inline.s: Excerpted from
A Discourse on Buddha-Recitation
If a deluded thought arises, this is karma coming to bind the mind;
By
replacing it with the Buddha-name, one transforms karma through the mind.
Karma is created by the mind, and karma turns with the mind.

The Twelfth Patriarch of the Pure Land school, Master Chewu, left a passage of instruction on “the mind can transform karma” that is extremely incisive. Those who practice Buddha-recitation should rely on it to dissolve old karma in accord with conditions and never create new misfortune. I now annotate this instruction below:

[The mind can create karma, and the mind can transform karma. Karma is created by the mind, and karma turns with the mind. If the mind cannot transform karma, it is bound by karma; if karma does not turn with the mind, it can bind the mind. How can the mind transform karma?
When the mind accords with the Way and the mind accords with the Buddha, it can transform karma.

How can karma bind the mind? When the mind relies on its habitual nature and acts and receives in accord with its drifting impulses, it is bound by karma. All the realms that appear before it and all the retributions to come are all perceived solely through karma and manifested solely by the mind.]

The mind can create karma, and the mind can transform karma. Karma is created by the mind, and karma is also turned by the mind. If the mind cannot transform karma, it is controlled by karma; if karma is not turned by the mind, it can control the mind. So how can the mind transform karma? When the mind accords with the Way and the mind accords with the Buddha, it can transform karma. How then can karma control the mind? If the mind still follows its usual habits and drifts along with the stream in what it does and what it receives, then it is bound by karma. All the realms that appear before it and all the retributions to come are perceived solely through karma and manifested solely by the mind.
[Binding the mind]That is, to control the mind.

For example, to hear slander and not become angry is to transform karma by the mind; to hear slander and become angry is karma coming to bind the mind. An ancient worthy said: “Accord with conditions to dissolve old karma, and by no means create new misfortune.” If the mind transforms karma, this is dissolving old karma; if karma binds the mind, this is creating new misfortune. Whether karma is dissolved or created, and whether one's fortune rises or falls, all hang upon this single thought. Right on the crest of the wave is the very time to do the practice and to test the practice!

[All is perceived solely through karma, therefore the realms that come and the retributions that arrive all have a certain measure, because karma can bind the mind. All is manifested solely by the mind, therefore the realms that come and the retributions that arrive all have no certain measure, because the mind can transform karma. If a person, precisely when karma is able to bind the mind and the realm before him and the retribution to come are fixed, suddenly rouses a vast mind, cultivates true practice, accords the mind with the Buddha and the mind with the Way, then the mind can transform karma, and the realm before him and the retribution to come, though fixed, are not fixed. Again, when the mind can transform karma and the realm before him and the retribution to come are not fixed, if the vast mind suddenly retreats and true practice is deficient, then karma can bind the mind, and the realm before him and the retribution to come, though not fixed, become fixed.]

Because all the realms are perceived solely through karma, so when circumstances appear and retribution arrives, there is a certain measure — this is because karma can control the mind. Because all the realms are manifested solely by the mind, so when circumstances appear and retribution arrives, there is no certain measure — this is because the mind can transform karma. If a person, precisely when karma is able to control the mind and the circumstances before him and the retribution to come are fixed, suddenly rouses the bodhi mind, cultivates true practice, accords the mind with the Buddha and the mind with the Way, then the mind can transform karma, and the circumstances before him and the retribution to come, though fixed, are not fixed. Again, when the mind can transform karma and the circumstances before him and the retribution to come are not fixed, if the vast mind suddenly retreats and true practice is deficient, then karma can control the mind, and the circumstances before him and the retribution to come, though not fixed, become fixed.

Yet karma was created in the past, and in that there is nothing to be done; fortunately, whether one rouses the mind or not — the pivot lies in myself. To create karma or to transform karma does not depend on another.]

Yet karma was created in the past and cannot be undone; fortunately, whether one rouses the mind and whether one's practice is genuine — the initiative lies in myself. When circumstances appear, whether to create new misfortune or dissolve old karma is likewise all up to me, and not up to another.

The coming of circumstances is the effect of old karma, but how one responds — the initiative is in oneself. Yet it is not that however one wishes to respond one can respond, and however one wishes to transform karma one can transform karma. It is like going to war: who does not wish to win? The key lies in strength. Therefore, to be able to respond correctly to circumstances, one must rouse the bodhi mind, cultivate true practice, accord the mind with the Buddha and the mind with the Way, and only then have the strength to transform karma and transform circumstances. This passage of Master Chewu sets forth the principle of transforming one's fate. One should savor it repeatedly and practice it without cease. Constantly examine oneself:
Is this karma binding the mind, or is this the mind transforming karma?

Remember: when circumstances appear, this is karma coming to bind the mind, requiring you to receive retribution and to create new misfortune; when the mind rests upon the Buddha-name and is not drawn along by them, this is the mind transforming karma (no retribution, or a light one), and dissolving old karma — weakening and even pulling up the karmic seeds in the ālayavijñāna.
[Just as we now rouse the mind to recite the Buddha, seeking rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Whether one contemplates the dependent and primary retributions, or holds fast to the Name,
thought after thought continuing without break

. When contemplation and recitation reach their extreme, the mind accords with the Buddha; accord upon accord, reaching the ultimate of accord, the mind can transform karma. And the Saha realm before one is transformed into the Land of Ultimate Bliss; the retribution of the womb-prison is transformed into the lotus womb. Then one is a free person of the Land of Bliss! If, precisely at this moment, the mind is occasionally lost, or suddenly gives rise to remorse, and does not accord with the Buddha, then karma can bind the mind, and the realm remains as before, the retribution to come as before — still a suffering being of the endurance world.]

Just as we now rouse the mind to recite the Buddha, seeking rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Whether we contemplate the dependent and primary splendor of the Land of Ultimate Bliss (as in the various contemplations of the Sutra of Contemplation on the Buddha of Measureless Life), or hold fast to the Name, thought after thought continuing without break (not interrupted by deluded thoughts). When contemplation and recitation reach their extreme, the mind accords with the Buddha; accord upon accord, reaching the ultimate of accord, the mind can transform karma. Thus the realm of the Saha world is transformed into the realm of the Land of Ultimate Bliss; the retribution of the womb-prison at death is transformed into birth by transformation in the lotus womb. Then one is indeed a free person of the Land of Ultimate Bliss! If, precisely when circumstances come with retribution, the mind is occasionally lost, or suddenly gives rise to remorse, and does not accord with the Buddha, then karma can bind the mind, and the realm remains as before, the retribution to come as before — still a suffering being of the endurance world.

[Dependent and primary retributions]Dependent retribution and primary retribution. The realms, lands, houses, and utensils of the world, upon which the body relies, are called dependent retribution; the body itself, which is the effect of past karma, is called primary retribution. [Endurance world]The Saha world; “Saha” is translated as “endurance.”
Master Chewu here reveals the secret of transforming karma:

“Whether one contemplates the dependent and primary retributions, or holds fast to the Name, thought after thought continuing without break. When contemplation and recitation reach their extreme, the mind accords with the Buddha; accord upon accord, reaching the ultimate of accord, the mind can transform karma.”
Please note:
thought after thought continuing without break
— this is the key.
Therefore, when recitation reaches the point of mutual response, not only will one surely be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss at death, but one can also transform one's own destiny right now.
Then we who are determined to leave behind and seek rebirth in the Pure Land — how can we not be roused to vigilance and roused to action!]

Then, having understood this principle, we who are determined to leave the Saha world and seek rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss — how can we not diligently apply ourselves and advance with all our might?

Question: It was said above that a person who recites the Buddha, with thought after thought continuing without break, can thereby transform karma by the mind. Then how does a Chan practitioner transform karma by the mind?

Answer: It was stated above that “when the mind accords with the Way, the mind can transform karma.” Not being driven by deluded, inverted thoughts, there is no cause for creating karma, because deluded thought is the cause of all karma;
if at the very place where a deluded thought arises one cuts it off in a single thought, the karmic roots accumulated of old are eliminated on the spot
. Therefore,
dwelling in stillness and yet fully illuminating, not turning with thoughts, not drawn by states,

one can transform karma by the mind. When you are now in “accepting the present moment, fully present, within not turning with thoughts, without not drawn by states,” you are in the state of seeing the nature in still, knowing awareness. (Regarding presence, see
The Chan of Awareness
) The Sixth Patriarch said:
“Not apart from the self-nature is the field of merit.”
The Essential Mind-Cultivation says:

“One who awakens to this and guards it sits in single suchness and, unmoving, is liberated; one who is deluded about this and turns away from it goes to the six destinies and transmigrates through long kalpas.”
(See
The Detailed Explanation of the Essential Mind-Cultivation
The Sutra of Contemplation on the Practice of Universal Worthy Bodhisattva's Dharma says:

“The ocean of all karmic hindrances arises entirely from deluded thought. If one wishes to repent, sit upright and contemplate true reality. The many offenses are like frost and dew, which the sun of wisdom can melt away.”
Master Hanshan said:

“Now, if one wishes old karma to be eliminated, one must first bring forth the great light of wisdom, illumine and break apart ignorance, and not allow deluded thought to sprout and grow secretly in the dark;
if at the very place where a deluded thought arises one cuts it off in a single thought, the karmic roots accumulated of old are eliminated on the spot

. This is what is meant by ‘do not fear the arising of thoughts, only fear the lateness of awakening.’ If one’s illuminating awareness is the least bit late, one is turned about by it. If, in the place where thoughts arise in daily use, one is aware of each thought and extinguishes each thought, this is what is meant by ‘the many offenses are like frost and dew, which the sun of wisdom can melt away.’ Because
(because)
the darkness of ignorance can be broken only by wisdom — this is what is meant by wisdom being able to eliminate. If
(you)

day and night without cease diligently observe, never letting it pass, and at the very place where deluded thought arises thoroughly investigate it, so that there is no mark of arising at all. Look and look again, and ultimately it is unobtainable. After long practice and full familiarity, one’s own mind is pure and without anything in it,
and the mind without anything is true reality

. If one constantly contemplates this mind, what deluded thought could be harbored, and what accumulated karma could lodge there? To apply the mind in this way is called the samādhi of illuminating contemplation.”
(From the Dream Travels Collection
Instruction to Dong Zhiguang)

[If, day and night without cease, diligently observe]Here the “if” means you. For example: “What would it be like to exchange your task of catching snakes and restore your taxes?” (This sentence comes from Liu Zongyuan's “The Snake Catcher”; the translation: to exchange your task of catching poisonous snakes and restore your taxes — what do you think?)
